free_tier.stated: A build-only challenge on N-ATLAS, Nigeria's open-source multilingual model (Llama-3 8B fine-tuned for Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo and Nigerian-accented English), whose listed benefits include 'Compute credits through partner infrastructure' and an 'N-ATLAS co-contributor credit'. No cash or GPU-hour amount is published on the page read.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The compute benefit is a credit on partner infrastructure, and the partner named elsewhere in the same programme family is Galaxy Backbone, which means the credit is only useful inside Nigeria's national data centre network rather than on a commercial cloud.

limits.value: The general requirement reads 'All team members must be Nigerian citizens or registered Nigerian entities', and the Innovation & Enterprise track adds 'Individual applicants must be Nigerian citizens aged 18 or above', so citizenship is checked before any compute is discussed.

evidence.proved: 'All team members must be Nigerian citizens or registered Nigerian entities'; 'Individual applicants must be Nigerian citizens aged 18 or above'; 'Company applicants must be registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission', quoted
benefits list 'Compute credits through partner infrastructure' and 'N-ATLAS co-contributor credit', quoted
page description reads 'Deadline: 12 October 2026', and the page states 'Applications Open 22 September 2026 | Deadline 12 October 2026', quoted
'Diaspora teams must have at least 50% of members based in Nigeria', quoted

record.notes: Two things are unsettled and both matter. First, the amount: the page names compute credits without a quantity, so the finding carries a null rather than an estimate. Second, the deadline of 12 October 2026 had passed ten days before this read, and no successor round is published. The 50 percent in-Nigeria rule for diaspora teams is the only clause that contemplates non-resident members, and it still requires a Nigerian majority.
